title: Global Tech IPOs: Preparing for Potential Market Pressure on Indian Stocks
description: A prominent investor warns that 2027 could see significant pressure on US stock markets. This pressure is attributed to a potential surge in major tech IPOs, .

faq.q: Will Indian markets crash if US markets fall significantly?
faq.a: While Indian markets are not immune to global shocks, a direct "crash" is not guaranteed. A significant US market correction could lead to FII outflows and negative sentiment, causing Indian markets to correct, but India's strong domestic growth story often provides some resilience.

faq.q: Should I sell all my equity investments now?
faq.a: No, making drastic decisions like selling all your equity investments based on a warning is generally not advisable. Such actions often lead to missing out on subsequent recoveries. Instead, review your asset allocation and make measured adjustments.

faq.q: How do FIIs affect Indian stocks during global volatility?
faq.a: Foreign Institutional Investors (FIIs) tend to withdraw capital from emerging markets like India when global markets face pressure, leading to selling pressure on Indian equities and potentially causing market corrections.

faq.q: Is this a good time to invest in international funds?
faq.a: If you currently lack international diversification, a period of potential correction in global markets could present an opportunity to start or increase investments in international funds through SIPs, averaging out your entry cost.

faq.q: What role does the RBI play in such scenarios?
faq.a: The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) monitors global economic developments closely. It can intervene through monetary policy tools, such as adjusting interest rates or managing currency, to stabilise the Indian economy, control inflation, and support financial stability.

faq.q: How can I protect my portfolio from global volatility?
faq.a: Protecting your portfolio involves diversification across asset classes (equity, debt, gold), investing in fundamentally strong companies, maintaining an adequate emergency fund, and regularly rebalancing your portfolio to your target asset allocation.
